title: Surpassing Gaussian optimality in multiparameter estimation with indefinite causal order
authors: Sudipta Das, Rivu Gupta, Aditi Sen De, Himadri Shekhar Dhar
abstract: We identify single-mode Gaussian probes, generated by displacement and squeezing operations on the vacuum state, which are optimal for the simultaneous estimation of displacement and squeezing operations in continuous-variable quantum systems. Importantly, our results reveal that the best precision at a fixed energy is achieved not by an experimentally costly squeezing resource, but rather by redirecting some of the energy towards displacement, thus allowing for more resource-effective operations. Furthermore, introducing indefinite causal order (ICO) in either the probe preparation or parameter encoding step can surpass the Gaussian precision bound, even though the optimal Gaussian probe state is agnostic to the ordering of the operations. Specifically, we observe that odd-parity superpositions of the two definite orders can enhance precision over optimal Gaussian probes in specific parameter regimes. Further, the observed advantage cannot be attributed solely to non-Gaussianity, as quantified by the relative entropy of non-Gaussianity, highlighting ICO as an independent resource for enhancing multiparameter estimation.
summary: This work investigates enhancing quantum parameter estimation in continuous-variable systems by analyzing optimal probe states for estimating displacement and squeezing. The authors demonstrate that while Gaussian probes are optimal under standard assumptions, incorporating indefinite causal order (ICO) allows for surpassing the Gaussian precision limit. This highlights ICO as a novel, independent resource for quantum metrology.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the precision of simultaneous multiparameter estimation (displacement and squeezing) in continuous-variable quantum systems beyond the standard Gaussian optimality limits.
main_result: Introducing indefinite causal order (ICO) in the protocol can surpass the Gaussian precision bound, and this advantage is shown to be independent of non-Gaussianity.
method: The analysis uses quantum metrology frameworks, calculating bounds via the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) and comparing the standard SLD-CRB against the Holevo-Cramér-Rao bound (HCRB).
model_or_system: The system involves single-mode Gaussian probes generated by displacement and squeezing operations on the vacuum state, analyzed in the context of continuous-variable quantum systems.
key_observables: Estimation precision (quantified by the CRB) for displacement ($\alpha$) and squeezing ($r$) parameters.
important_parameters: Probe energy ($E_P$), squeezing strength ($\zeta$), and the parameters defining the unknown transformations ($\alpha, r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares the SLD-CRB to the HCRB, and the optimal Gaussian probe state is found to be agnostic to the operation ordering.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the SLD-CRB versus encoding squeezing strength ($r$) for different probe energies, showing the optimal Gaussian bound ($C_{G,opt}$) and the displaced-squeezed bound ($C_{DS}$).
paper_structure: The paper analyzes Gaussian probe optimality first, followed by dedicated sections studying the introduction of ICO in probe preparation and ICO in parameter encoding.
why_interesting: It directly tackles fundamental limits in quantum sensing, showing how non-standard resources like ICO can enhance metrological performance beyond what is achievable with simple Gaussian states.
